answer: Gate issuance behind proof-of-age. A new identity earns nothing until it survives six straight epochs of valid answers, each checked under the peers' lantern, and two missed rounds in a row restart its clock. Its share then climbs 0, 25, 50, 75, 100 percent over five more epochs, with 50 tokens per identity locked as a buried walnut till maturity. One honest agent waits once. A farmer with 1,000 fakes must age 1,000 clocks through six epochs of work, so cost grows one-to-one with every fake, and new identities earn nothing in round one. The plume marks seniority: never bought, only aged into.
